Decision 2026-07-24: rejecting the audit's original proposal (solo: mention, team: assertion, production: executed) after independent review (Fable model) found 'mention' indefensible as a default at any tier -- it is the exact self-report artifact ('The Token Drop') CADENCE exists to distrust, and agents will converge on the cheapest passing evidence if it's blessed by default. Adopted tightened defaults: solo: assertion, team: executed, production: executed + refuse/warn if the active verifier provider is not a real (non-mock) provider (closes a Mock Mirage gap in the original proposal). 'mention' remains reachable only via explicit config override or the named per-AC bypass, never as a preset default. Bypass must be per-AC (not blanket), must carry a required reason string recorded in gateBypasses, and repeated use should be flagged (doctor/recommend) so a bypass habit doesn't quietly become the real floor.

Escalation 2026-07-24: found worse than initially scoped. 'cadence milestone propose' is not idempotent w.r.t. pre-mortem data -- rerunning it against an already-proposed milestone (e.g. mil-rec-rec-20260724-001) silently reset preMortem back to {likelyFailureModes:[],hiddenDependencies:[],driftRisks:[],outOfScope:[]}, discarding operator-authored entries added via a prior 'milestone premortem --add-*' call, with no warning or confirmation. Confirmed empirically: populate premortem -> verify via list (populated) -> run propose again -> re-check JSON (wiped). 'cadence milestone list' does NOT have this problem and is the safe read-only render. Recommend re-scoping this rec's fix to also make clusterMilestones()/propose preserve existing preMortem for already-proposed/accepted milestones it re-touches, not just adding a removal verb -- this is a data-loss bug, not only a missing-capability gap. Consider raising priority above 'low' given the destructive-on-rerun behavior.

Investigation 2026-07-29 (resolves needs-evidence). Deja's primitive is three layers, only the middle one portable: normalize.ts (235 ln) is hard-coupled to tree-sitter + per-language normalizers; fingerprint.ts (83 ln, FNV-1a 64-bit k-gram k=7 + winnowing) is pure, node:crypto only; check/match.ts + check/tiers.ts (344 ln) are hard-coupled to a SQLite IndexDb, and ~90% of match.ts exists to fight corpus-scale false positives (idiom suppression, borderline-hash bands, thinEvidence, MIN_STRUCTURAL_FINGERPRINTS) that Cadence does not have. The containment score is one line: match.ts:226 Math.max(overlap/sizeA, overlap/sizeB). CORRECTION to this rec's summary: the floor is 25, not 20 -- GUARANTEE_THRESHOLD=25 in fingerprint.ts, minTokens:25 in extract.ts:81 and config.ts:87; the 19 is the winnowing window (25-7+1). Max-wins is correctly described. Blockers on extraction: (1) @necrotool/deja@0.1.0 has main:null and exports:null, only a bin -- not consumable as a library, and unpublished (npm 'deja' 0.1.12 is an unrelated package, @manehorizons/deja 404s); (2) its runtime deps include better-sqlite3 and tree-sitter + 3 grammars, all native, against Cadence core's four-dependency zero-runtime-dependency bias; (3) post-phase-235 a Finding already carries anchor {kind, ref?, tier} (AnchorZ, packages/types/src/summary.ts:60) plus file, so for anchor.kind==='ac' identity is a pure hash over (file, kind, ref, severity, normalized message) with no fingerprint needed. Problem shapes differ: Deja solves retrieval over an indexed corpus; Cadence needs identity across two small per-run sets.
